item.title: NETBALL FIJI REVIVAL I Northern rally sparks netball revival
item.description: The M-PAiSA Netball Fiji Rally is giving grassroots netball a major boost, with the strong response to the inaugural Northern leg in Savusavu sparking calls for the event to become an annual fixture. More than 30 teams took part in the Northern Rally last Friday, highlighting the depth of interest and talent in grassroots netball outside Fiji’s traditional competition centres.
item.content:encoded:
The M-PAiSA Netball Fiji Rally is giving grassroots netball a major boost, with the strong response to the inaugural Northern leg in Savusavu sparking calls for the event to become an annual fixture.

More than 30 teams took part in the Northern Rally last Friday, highlighting the depth of interest and talent in grassroots netball outside Fiji’s traditional competition centres.

For many young players, community competitions such as the M-PAiSA Rally are where their netball journeys begin. The opportunity to compete in a structured tournament provides players with valuable exposure, while giving them a platform to develop their skills and gain experience in competitive netball.

The rally has also brought communities together, with players, families and supporters turning out to celebrate the sport. The response in Savusavu has been particularly encouraging, with growing calls from the Northern community for the rally to return each year.

For Netball Fiji, that response reflects the wider objective of its revival ,strengthening the sport from the grassroots up and creating more opportunities for players across the country.

The partnership with M-PAiSA, operated by Digital Financial Services Pte Limited, a owned subsidiary of Vodafone Fiji, is also helping to strengthen that pathway. The rally marks M-PAiSA’s first sporting event sponsorship and represents an investment in creating opportunities for young women and men to participate in competitive sport, develop their abilities and potentially pursue professional sporting careers.

M-PAiSA General Manager Digital Financial Services, Shailendra Prasad, said the Northern Rally had provided strong momentum for the partnership.

“The Northern Rally was a successful start to our partnership with Netball Fiji. We expect even greater participation in the Central and Western rallies. This is about giving more players the opportunity to compete, develop their skills and take the next step in their netball journey.”

The momentum generated in the North now moves to the Central Division, with the next rally scheduled for Saturday, August 15, at the National Netball Centre in Suva.

The final rally will be held in the Western Division on Saturday, August 29, at Lautoka Central College.

The two remaining rallies are expected to build on the participation seen in Savusavu, with teams, supporters and communities encouraged to come out and support the players as they compete at centre court.

item.title: Nadi secures win
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi women’s team have broken new ground in the Subrails Marama Championship, ending their winless streak against Suva with a 32-24 triumph at HFC Bank National Stadium yesterday. The Nadi side arrived in the capital high on confidence following their 89-12 demolition of Lautoka last week, but it was their fitness and willingness to attack from anywhere that proved decisive.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi women’s team have broken new ground in the Subrails Marama Championship, ending their winless streak against Suva with a 32-24 triumph at HFC Bank National Stadium yesterday.

The Nadi side arrived in the capital high on confidence following their 89-12 demolition of Lautoka last week, but it was their fitness and willingness to attack from anywhere that proved decisive.

They took the game to Suva from the opening whistle, stretching the home defence with a fast and expansive style of rugby.

Four first-half tries against Suva’s one gave Nadi a commanding 20-7 lead at halftime.

Suva refused to surrender and came out firing after the break, scoring early to turn the contest into a seesaw battle.

The visitors lifted the tempo in the final quarter, eventually pulling clear to secure a historic victory.

Nadi captain and openside flanker Laisa Seru said the team had been warned against underestimating their opponents.

“Every week the message is always not to underestimate any team,” Seru said.

“Of course the Suva girls have a lot of experience but we backed our fitness today and it paid off for us, I think.”

Seru credited the players for their determination to finish strongly.

“The coach told us just to come out here and give it our all and finish the game on a high,” she said.

“We were psyched up a little bit but we are very grateful to the girls for not giving up and finishing the game strong.”

Despite the historic win, Seru knows Nadi cannot afford to become complacent.

“Lots of positive and a lot of work still to do,” she said.

“We will go back on Monday and look at our weaknesses and get ready for the next game.”

In other Marama Championship fixtures today, Tailevu will face Nadroga at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori at 1pm. Kadavu will host Rewa at the Namalata School ground in Vunisea, also at 1pm, while Macuata takes on Ba at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka at 11am.

At Thompson Park in Navua, Namosi will host Nasinu at 1pm, while Lautoka battles Naitasiri at Churchill Park, at 11am.

item.title: North’s quest
item.description: HISTORY has taken Navatu Secondary School this far. This afternoon, the north gets its chance to demand more. When Navatu runs onto the field for its Vodafone Super Deans under-19 semi-final against Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), it will carry something far heavier than a rugby ball and the weight of expectation.
item.content:encoded:
HISTORY has taken Navatu Secondary School this far. This afternoon, the north gets its chance to demand more.

When Navatu runs onto the field for its Vodafone Super Deans under-19 semi-final against Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), it will carry something far heavier than a rugby ball and the weight of expectation.

It will carry the pride of an entire region.

For a school that does not have its own rugby ground or gymnasium, simply reaching the national semi-finals is an extraordinary achievement.

But Navatu is not travelling this far to make up the numbers.

The boys have already toppled one of the southern zone’s established giants Suva Grammar School.

Now they stand 80 minutes from a place in the Deans final and within touching distance of creating a moment that could change the way northern schoolboy rugby is viewed.

For principal Kiniviliame Naciqa, this journey is about much more than one rugby team.

“This victory means far more than reaching a semi-final. It represents belief, hard work, discipline, sacrifice and unity,” Naciqa said.

“It shows that northern students can compete with the best in the country and has become a source of pride and inspiration for the entire North.”

The quarter-final victory over Suva Grammar was the defining statement.

It showed that Navatu’s rise was not built on reputation or resources, but on the character of its players.

“It showed the character, resilience and belief of our boys,” Naciqa said.

“They trusted their preparation, stayed disciplined and worked for each other.”

item.title: LMS’s dynasty or NSS’s redemption
item.description: LELEAN Memorial School is chasing the return of an old order. Nasinu Secondary School is chasing something it has never quite managed to achieve.
item.content:encoded:
LELEAN Memorial School is chasing the return of an old order.

Nasinu Secondary School is chasing something it has never quite managed to achieve.

And when the two meet this afternoon in the Vodafone Super Deans under-18 semi-final at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, history will be on the line.

For Lelean, the semi-final represents another step towards restoring the stature of a school that once dominated Fiji secondary school rugby.

The Davuilevu-based school was once the ultimate Deans dynasty — a name synonymous with success and a team every other school measured itself against.

Now, as Eastern Zone champions, Lelean has an opportunity to begin another era.

Its quarter-final performance suggested it has the ingredients to do just that.

Lelean dismantled Ratu Navula College 26-5 last Saturday, leading 10-0 at halftime before turning the screws after the break.

Their forwards dominated the breakdown and forced Ratu Navula into a series of penalties.

Fullback Ratu Apenisa Navikutu then kept his composure in difficult conditions, landing two crucial penalties before inside centre Joseva Atanj powered over late to put the result beyond doubt.

It was a performance that underlined Lelean’s credentials as a genuine title contender.

But this is a team that has learned to live with pressure.

Nasinu wants to ensure this is the year its persistence finally produces silverware.

And neither side will be satisfied with simply making the final.

This afternoon, preparation, discipline and composure will be tested when the two sides collide with a place in the Deans final at stake.

For Lelean, the road back to dynasty continues.

For Nasinu, the road to redemption runs through Davuilevu’s old giants.

By the final whistle, one of those journeys will end.

The other will move one step closer to Deans glory.

item.title: Champions face tough golf challenge
item.description: The fairways are prepped, the clubs are polished, and the rivalries are officially brewing. Today, the Fiji Society for the Blind’s Annual Charity Ambrose Golf Tournament tees off at the Fiji Golf Club with over 84 golfers.
item.content:encoded:
The fairways are prepped, the clubs are polished, and the rivalries are officially brewing.

Today, the Fiji Society for the Blind’s Annual Charity Ambrose Golf Tournament tees off at the Fiji Golf Club with over 84 golfers.

While the ultimate goal is raising hope and vital funds for Fijians living with blindness or low vision, make no mistake – the competition on the greens is going to be fierce.

All eyes are on four standout teams, each bringing their own flavor of intensity to the tournament.

First up is “4 Irons”, made up of Eroni Mavoa, George Nacewa, David Qiolevu and Lusi Leqa, the champions from a charity ambrose tournament last month.

They arrive with targets on their backs, carrying the quiet confidence of players who know exactly what it takes to win. They aren’t just looking for a good time; they’re looking for a repeat.

“We know the course, and we know the pressure,” says captain Eroni Mavoa.

“Obviously, we didn’t come here to make numbers. We came to remind everyone why we are champions.”

Looking to dethrone them is the Fiji Times team, a powerhouse squad led by the formidable Sikipio Fihaki, the 2001 Suva Grammar Deans winner.

His teammates are Jai Lal, Suresh Prasad and Steven Yam. Known for their strategic play, this team has been the talk of the tournament hosts, Pirates Golf Club all week.

They have the talent, the drive, and a singular focus on taking the top spot.

“Respect to the ‘4 Irons’, but past victories don’t sink putts today,” Sikipio Fihaki states flatly.

“My team is dialed in. We’re leaving everything on the course, and we’re walking away with the win.”

And then there is Marsh, the wild cards led by the tournament’s own Auctioneer and MC, Wayne Wong, alongside Tomasi Tuitoga, Lewis Sahai and Eric Nand.

What they might lack in pure intimidation, they make up for in sheer momentum and unshakeable team spirit. Wayne is known for working a crowd, but tomorrow, he’s ready to work the fairway.

“Let the other guys and gals stress over their swings,” Wayne laughs.

“We’re playing with heart, we’re playing for the cause, and we’re going to steal this tournament right out from under them while they’re busy over-thinking.”

The fourth team is Shipping Services – an all women’s team made up of Barbara Naisara, Soni Matthews, Loata Maraia and Merelita McCarthy, the Fiji Golf Club Championship women winner.

They bring a refreshing mix of precision, composure, and quiet determination.

“We’re here to show that women belong at the top of the leaderboard just as much as anyone else,” says Merelita McCarthy.

“Every drive and every putt is proof that strength, skill, and heart have no gender. Tomorrow, we’re not just playing golf – we’re playing to inspire.”

It’s the perfect storm of skill, strategy, and swagger. Whether it’s the proven champions, the strategic powerhouse, the spirited underdogs, or the trailblazing women’s team, tomorrow’s tournament promises fireworks on the course.

Who will emerge victorious? The only way to find out is to be there. Join us tomorrow at the Fiji Golf Club, come for the golf, stay for the cause, and witness a tournament to remember.

item.title: For the Vanua | Ra’s rise to test Grammar’s pride
item.description: RA High School’s remarkable Vodafone Super Deans under-18 campaign reaches its biggest test yet when it faces Southern Zone powerhouse Suva Grammar School in the semi-final at Churchill Park, Lautoka, this weekend. For Ra, this is no longer simply about a school chasing a place in the Deans final.
item.content:encoded:
RA High School’s remarkable Vodafone Super Deans under-18 campaign reaches its biggest test yet when it faces Southern Zone powerhouse Suva Grammar School in the semi-final at Churchill Park, Lautoka, this weekend.

For Ra, this is no longer simply about a school chasing a place in the Deans final.

It is about a rugby community beginning to believe.

The boys from Ra have emerged as the surprise package of the competition, knocking out traditional powerhouse and defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School in the quarter-final to earn their place among the final four.

But their biggest strength could be what lies beyond the school gates. Ra rugby is enjoying a resurgence at provincial level.

The Ra Rugby Union recently secured the Vodafone Vanua Championship title and, with it, promotion to the Skipper Cup for the first time in its history.

Against Ra High will be a Grammar side accustomed to the big stage.

The Lions have the resources, experience, depth and structure that have made them one of the recognised powers of secondary school rugby. They also have unfinished business.

Grammar’s last Deans U18 title came in 2001 when they defeated Ratu Kadavulevu School 34-10.

Twenty-five years later, the Lions are again within two wins of the trophy.

Their latest step came with a convincing 23-7 victory over Ba Provincial Freebird Institute in the quarter-final, where their forwards laid the foundation before the backs finished the job.

Grammar will therefore enter the semi-final with confidence. But they will also know that Ra have already shown they cannot be judged by reputation or resources.

Ra may not possess the same traditional pedigree as Grammar, but it has belief, physicality and the growing support of an entire province behind it.

For the Ra players, every tackle and every carry will be watched by a community that has tasted success at provincial level and now wants its schoolboys to create another piece of history.

The winner will book a place in the Deans final. But for Ra, victory would mean something more. It would confirm that the province’s recent rugby breakthrough is not an isolated success.

It would be another sign that Ra rugby is moving forward, from the provincial field to the schoolboy stage.

Ra are no longer just playing for Ra High School but they are playing for the vanua of Ra.

item.title: From parents’ vision to the international stage
item.description: WHAT began as a vision among parents to give their daughters greater exposure has grown into an international opportunity for the under-15 Royale Rising Star from Nakoivalu Netball Academy. The team will make its first appearance at the International Netball Festival in Christchurch, New Zealand from August 26-28.
item.content:encoded:
WHAT began as a vision among parents to give their daughters greater exposure has grown into an international opportunity for the under-15 Royale Rising Star from Nakoivalu Netball Academy.

The team will make its first appearance at the International Netball Festival in Christchurch, New Zealand from August 26-28.

The team was formed by parents whose daughters have been playing club netball since they were 10 years old.

Academy founder Unaisi Ranavue said the idea was to bring the parents together and create an opportunity for the girls to experience international competition.

“The parents thought to come together to organise an international tour and to have an exposure for the International Netball Festival,” Ranavue said.

The team’s participation is also a milestone for the academy, which had previously only followed the tournament from afar.

“We’ve been hearing about it, but we’ve never been part of it,” she said.

“So, this is a milestone and a huge achievement for us to get registered and be part of the competition.”

The team is now preparing for the Christchurch challenge, with the players having completed strength and conditioning and core sessions before moving into court work.

Ranavue also said the experience would be about more than results, with the players gaining confidence and learning from competing at an international level.

The International Netball Festival is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year.

item.title: Fijiana name side for second Test
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV has named its starting side for Saturday’s second test against the Springbok women at Churchill Park in Lautoka, with several changes to the team that started the opening match. Karalaini Naisewa will start at prop, with Bitila Tawake(vice captain) and Keri Lawavou retaining the number two and three jerseys.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV has named its starting side for Saturday’s second test against the Springbok women at Churchill Park in Lautoka, with several changes to the team that started the opening match.

Karalaini Naisewa will start at prop, with Bitila Tawake(vice captain) and Keri Lawavou retaining the number two and three jerseys.

Jade Coates starts at lock alongside Karavaki Lutumaibau, while Nunia Daunimoala and Adi Salaseini Railumu retain their places in the loose forwards.

Merewairita Neivoha moves into the number seven jersey, with Adi Salaseini Railumu at number eight.

Kolora Lomani continues as captain at scrum-half, with Varanisese Qoro at fly-half.

At centre, Ruth Raketekete and Ivamere Rokowati will line up together, while Atelaite Buna and Adi Vani Buleki start on the wings.

Litiana Vueti retains the fullback position.

The changes come after Fijiana suffered a 55-12 defeat to South Africa in the opening Test in Suva last Saturday.

Reserves; Selai Naliva, Elesi Saukuru, Tiana Robanakadavu, Vilisi Tivalele, Sereana Maragi, Evivi Senikarivi, Adi Salote Nailolo, Vasemaca Duva.

Fijiana coach Willie Walker will be looking for a response from his players after identifying discipline, ball retention and defence as key areas for improvement following the first Test.
